narrative: Material PL1__MFDEA656 exhibits erratic but continuous demand (CV=0.349, 100% fill rate) with a mean of 4,185 units/day and no statistically significant trend. Lead times are unstable (CV=0.679), driving a high sigma_LTD of 4,624 units and a required safety stock of 7,607 units — far above the current SAP setting of 95. The (r,Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ-derived order quantity of 7,720 units efficiently balances ordering and holding costs, yielding a 19.5% annual cost reduction while maintaining 95% service level.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is erratic but continuous (non-zero fraction=100%), making a continuous-review reorder-point model appropriate. EOQ exceeds MOQ so the minimum order quantity constraint is non-binding. Unstable lead times make it critical to hold sufficient safety stock rather than relying on safety lead time alone.
research_insights.boundary_risk: No capacity constraint binds: SS (7,607) + OQ (7,720) = 15,327 units, well below max_storage_units (45,030). No service-level or cost risk from capacity.
